appliedObject.name: Hadeland Glassverk
appliedObject.finding: The stable named Hadeland Glassverk point lies within the production and visitor complex and provides a place-specific anchor for the whole institution rather than one shop, park feature or assumed workshop centroid.

officialVisitorContext.sourceName: Hadeland Glassverk – opening hours and visitor information
officialVisitorContext.finding: The official visitor page identifies the site as a living experience centre with shops, dining, activities, museum and glassblowing at Glassverksveien 9.

officialIndustrialIdentity.finding: The official history identifies the glassworks as founded in 1762 at Jevnaker by Randsfjorden and describes the development from bottles and household glass to design and art glass.

productionCoreContext.finding: The official site calls Glasshytta the heart of the operation and documents continuing glass production, glassblowing, grinding and polishing. No stable building geometry for Glasshytta was captured, so it is retained as functional context rather than used as an invented coordinate.

areaCrossCheck.name: Hadeland Glassverk
areaCrossCheck.finding: The named park object confirms the wider public complex around the glassworks but is not the industrial institution or production building itself.

independentEntityCrossCheck.finding: Wikidata independently identifies Hadeland Glassverk as a glassworks and company founded in 1762 at Jevnaker, but its coordinate is too coarse for production use.

radiusDecision.finding: The retained radius covers the named glassworks point, the nearby public park and the central production, museum and visitor complex.

decision.representationLimit: The marker represents the named glassworks institution and central visitor-production complex. The radius is not a property boundary, legal heritage polygon, exact industrial-site geometry or claim that the park or one retail building represents the full works.
